speaker: Doctor
text: I see you have double vision, difficulty climbing stairs, and upper limb weakness; to narrow this down, do you notice any drooping eyelids or slurred speech? Also, does your double vision improve when you close one eye?

speaker: Patient
text: The double vision usually happens when I look up or down, and the weakness in my arms and legs gets worse after activity but improves if I rest. I have not noticed balance problems or numbness.

speaker: Doctor
text: That fluctuation pattern is very concerning for myasthenia gravis; do you experience significant fatigue after chewing or swallowing? Also, have you ever noticed any drooping of your eyelids or difficulty keeping your eyes open for long periods?

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had recent infections or fevers, and there is no family history of neurological disease. The weakness feels symmetrical in both arms and legs.
